original_value: In this paper, an adaptive contrast enhancement method based on the neighborhood conditional histogram is proposed to improve the visual quality of thermal infrared images. Existing block-based local contrast enhancement methods usually suffer from the over-enhancement of smooth regions or the loss of some details. To address these drawbacks, we first introduce a neighborhood conditional histogram to adaptively enhance the contrast and avoid the over-enhancement caused by the original histogram. Then the clip-redistributed histogram of the contrast-limited adaptive histogram equalization (CLAHE) is replaced by the neighborhood conditional histogram. In addition, the local mapping function of each sub-block is updated based on the global mapping function to further eliminate the block artifacts. Lastly, the optimized local contrast enhancement process, which combines both global and local enhanced results is employed to obtain the desired enhanced result. Experiments are conducted to evaluate the performance of the proposed method and the other five methods are introduced as a comparison. Qualitative and quantitative evaluation results demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms the other block-based methods on local contrast enhancement, visual quality improvement, and noise suppression.

result.paraphrase: This paper proposes an adaptive contrast enhancement approach based on a neighborhood conditional histogram to improve the visual quality of thermal infrared images. Conventional block-based local contrast enhancement methods often over-enhance smooth areas or lose some details. To overcome these issues, a neighborhood conditional histogram is first introduced to adaptively enhance contrast and prevent the over-enhancement caused by the original histogram. Next, the clip-redistributed histogram in contrast-limited adaptive histogram equalization (CLAHE) is replaced with the neighborhood conditional histogram. In addition, each sub-block’s local mapping function is updated according to the global mapping function to further reduce block artifacts. Finally, an optimized local contrast enhancement procedure that combines the global and local enhancement results is used to produce the desired output. Experiments are carried out to assess the proposed method, with five other methods included for comparison. Both qualitative and quantitative results show that the proposed method surpasses the other block-based methods in local contrast enhancement, visual quality improvement, and noise suppression.
